LESSON: GOVERNMENT REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: GOVERNANCE
Topic 5.2: Government Revenue and Expenditure

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Government Revenue and Expenditure. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we pay taxes to the government?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya
2. explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue
3. identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya
4. explain the meaning of key words in the preamble

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: GOVERNMENT REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES · Grade: Grade 6
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Government Revenue and Expenditure helps you succeed in SOCIAL STUDIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

KEY FACTS: GOVERNMENT REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE
Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.
Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.
Rights come with responsibilities.

PART 1: Identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Government Revenue and Expenditure” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue

What this means
In this part you learn to explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain: Give one cause and one effect linked to Government Revenue and Expenditure.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Participate: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Explain the meaning of key words in the preamble

What this means
In this part you learn to explain the meaning of key words in the preamble. You will use ideas from in your county, school, and Kenyan community.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain the meaning of key words in the preamble.
2. Locate, explain, then act responsibly using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Locate: Connect “Government Revenue and Expenditure” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home).

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain the meaning of key words in the preamble. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Government Revenue and Expenditure is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Good citizens follow rules, respect others, and care for shared places.

Kenyan examples: lining up, keeping the compound clean, telling the truth, helping a classmate.

Example 1: Connect “Government Revenue and Expenditure” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya)

Example 2: Give one cause and one effect linked to Government Revenue and Expenditure. (skill: explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue)

Example 3: Describe one responsible action a Grade learner can take. (skill: identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya)

Example 4: Connect “Government Revenue and Expenditure” to a real place or group in Kenya (school, market, county office, home). (skill: explain the meaning of key words in the preamble)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Government Revenue and Expenditure to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya.
3. Practise this skill: explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue.
4. Practise this skill: identify key words in the preamble of the Constitution of Kenya.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Government Revenue and Expenditure from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Government Revenue and Expenditure: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 6 learner study Government Revenue and Expenditure?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we pay taxes to the government?
2. What is the importance of the preamble in the Constitution of Kenya?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Government Revenue and Expenditure means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify sources of revenue for National Government in Kenya.
5. Be able to: explain ways in which the national and county governments in Kenya spend their revenue.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
